messages.content:
Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 74
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: Latin American
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Pharmacist
  trauma_type: Physical abuse by romantic partner
  pcl5: 66

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Family-Related Comments: Comments on family, Emotional Closeness: Someone getting emotionally close to me, Auditory (Door): Doors opening or slamming
  Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Own Body: Paying attention to or looking at my own body, Avoid Feelings: Allowing myself to feel any strong emotion, Avoid People: avoid other people
  Threat: Body on Alert: My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger, Intrusion Monitoring: I listen for sounds that might mean someone is entering my home, Alert at Home: I feel on guard even inside my own home
  Memory: Bodily Reenactment: When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred., Snapshot Memory: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind., Shame on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense shame
  Negative Appraisals: No Longer Capable: I am no longer capable of doing the things that defined me, Lost Faith: I have lost my faith in people, life, or a higher power, Weakness Belief: I am a weak person

Vignette:
Maria, a 74-year-old Latin American woman and pharmacist, has been living with the aftermath of severe physical abuse inflicted by her romantic partner over several years. The trauma began to surface when she was in her early sixties, but it wasn't until recently that Maria found herself unable to cope with the daily triggers and symptoms. The abusive relationship had left deep emotional scars and persistent fear within Maria. Her husband would often become violent during arguments, leaving her bruised and shaken. Over time, these incidents had eroded her sense of safety and trust in others. The trauma was particularly potent because it occurred within a context where she should have felt secure and loved. Since the end of her marriage several years ago, Maria has experienced numerous triggers that remind her of the abuse. Family-related comments from friends or family members often evoke intense distress, as do situations involving emotional closeness. The sound of doors opening or slamming can suddenly bring back vivid memories of those traumatic moments when she felt threatened and powerless. Maria’s maladaptive strategies have become deeply ingrained over time. She has learned to avoid paying attention to her body, feeling any strong emotions, and even interacting with other people whenever possible. These avoidance behaviors have led to significant changes in her daily life. For instance, her role as a pharmacist has been affected because she now avoids engaging with patients and colleagues, often finding excuses to stay away from social interactions at work. Her heightened sense of threat is palpable. Maria's body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger. She listens intently for any sounds that might indicate someone entering her home, and even inside her own house, she remains on high alert. This constant state of vigilance has taken a toll on her physical health and overall well-being. When memories of the abuse do come up, they often feel like snapshots—moments frozen in time. Maria can recall each moment as if it were a picture in her mind, and the bodily reenactment of these memories makes her feel as though she is reliving those frightening events. The intense shame that accompanies these recollections further isolates her from others. Maria has come to believe that she is no longer capable of doing the things that once defined her—her work as a pharmacist and her social connections. She has lost faith in people, life, and any higher power that might provide solace or comfort. The belief that she is weak adds another layer of distress, reinforcing her sense of vulnerability. The consequences of these avoidance behaviors have been profound. Her relationships with family members have become strained as she pulls away from them to avoid triggers. At work, her colleagues notice a marked change in her behavior and engagement, affecting both her professional performance and her social life at the pharmacy. Finally, after years of struggling silently, Maria has decided to seek help. What brought her to this decision was a particularly distressing incident where she found herself unable to engage with a patient who needed emotional support. Realizing that her condition was worsening and that she could no longer ignore it, she reached out for professional assistance. Maria is most afraid of being powerless again and losing control over her life. However, she also hopes that therapy will help her regain a sense of security and trust in herself and others. Through this process, Maria aims to reclaim her identity and find peace in the present without constantly reliving the past.
